registerPolicy: Two coherent registers chosen per path and held constant within the path. Service paths (P3, P4, P5, P6, P9): learner uses saya; address terms (Pak/Bu/Mbak/Mas) and Anda are optional and context-appropriate, never mandatory per turn; natural pronoun omission is allowed; softeners tolong/boleh/permisi/maaf. Friend paths (P1, P2, P7, P8, P10): learner uses saya or aku with kamu, or omits the pronoun where natural; no gue/lu/nggak/banget/dong/sih and no Malay (awak, sila, tandas, macam mana, boleh tak). Where the interlocutor addresses the learner, the author writes one natural term fitting the scene or none, never a literal 'Bapak/Ibu' slash. Standard natural spoken Indonesian: meN-/ber- where natives use them, natural clipped counter verbs (cari, bayar, tukar) where A2 already established them; no Jakartan slang morphology.
genderSafety: Indonesian has no grammatical gender; the only gender-coded items are address terms (Pak/Bu/Mbak/Mas/Bapak/Ibu). They never appear as required speech tokens, recall answers, cloze answers or trophies, and no learner line asserts the learner's gender. Captions may name the interlocutor's role (Barista, Petugas); the base-locale caption may use any gender. Where the learner addresses staff, the term matches the depicted interlocutor; where the learner is addressed, one natural term or none. A reviewed per-lesson accepted-variant list may add the alternate term or its omission when meaning and politeness are unchanged.
orthography: Standard Indonesian (EYD V): Latin, NFC, no diacritics. Numbers in words in spoken lines (tiga puluh, dua ratus ribu rupiah); digits allowed only in captions/situations. Nasal prefix spelling checked (meN- sandhi: menukar, mengganggu, membawa, menghemat). Loanwords Indonesians actually use (diskon, konfirmasi, garansi, kursus, jadwal) are correct Indonesian; each gets a per-lesson-id loanword exemption, never global. Hyphenated reduplication (kira-kira, hati-hati) allowed in lines but never as trophy, recall answer or speech token.

segmentation.youOne: Learner's first reply: 8-16 words, single sentence or two short sentences, ends with a completion that invites the follow-up (a question to the friend, or a request/statement to staff). Contains the trophy as a whitespace-bounded token and all three speech tokens.
segmentation.youTwo: Learner's second reply: 6-12 words; continuation (shape B), resolution (shape A) or accept-with-modification (shape C). Source of the 2-3 cloze blanks.
segmentation.chunks: 4-7 meaningful chunks whose concatenation with single ASCII spaces equals the first reply exactly, including punctuation on the last token of a chunk. Chunks are phrase-sized (prepositional phrase, verb phrase, connector + clause head), never single function words except a connector that is the lesson's target form.
segmentation.speechTokens: Three distinct lowercase whole-word tokens present in the first reply; content words or the staged connector; never Pak/Bu/Mbak/Mas/Bapak/Ibu/saya/Anda/kamu/aku. The trophy is normally one of them, but the author may choose three better tokens. Numbers as words are allowed tokens.
segmentation.trophyAnchoring: Trophy is a bare dictionary surface form (no -nya, -lah, -kah, ku-, -mu attached; no hyphen), appearing identically in the first learner reply and in its own pattern example. Derived forms (ter-, ke-an, di-, ber-) are allowed as trophies only when they are the lesson's staged form and carry a distinct meaning from any A1/A2 trophy (kehujanan, ketinggalan, tersesat, terbuat, diperiksa), never as a re-spelling of a taught word.
segmentation.acceptedInput: Exact canonical first reply; case-insensitive, punctuation-insensitive. Beyond that only explicitly reviewed per-lesson accepted variants that keep meaning, stance and addressee identical (e.g. ya/iya; saya/aku in friend paths; alternate or omitted address term where reviewed). No generic token-ignoring, no stance particles (sih, kok, dong) accepted, no rule-generated address swaps; Malay or slang substitutions rejected.

knownTraps: Atemporal verbs: every German/English past, perfect or future base clause must be licensed by an explicit time/aspect marker in the SAME target line (sudah/tadi/kemarin/waktu itu/dulu/pernah for past; akan/mau/nanti/besok/tahun depan/minggu depan for future). Sequencing connectors (lalu, kemudian, setelah itu, akhirnya) never license tense on their own; each P1 narration line carries its own marker or its base stays present tense. telah is recognition-only written register (interlocutor or pattern lines), never productive learner speech.
Passive di- requires agent with oleh only when agent is expressed; agentless di- passive is the natural default for processes (Paketnya sudah dikirim). Do not calque German 'wurde von'.
ter- has three readings (accidental: tersesat; stative result: terbuat; ability: terjangkau). Only the accidental and result readings are productive; ability reading is recognition-only.
Concession: walaupun/meskipun + clause and tetapi are never combined in one sentence as a calque of German 'obwohl ... aber'. Validator flags 'walaupun ... tetapi' co-occurrence.
Negation: tidak for verbs/adjectives, bukan for nouns/pronouns; cloze distractors may exploit this but recall must not.

Hypotheticals: kalau is neutral, jika slightly formal, seandainya counterfactual; sekiranya is formal written register and recognition-only at B1. Pairing seandainya with a realis consequence is wrong; P3 stages seandainya only from L7, P7 stays with kalau/jika/asalkan.
Relative yang clauses: possessive description is 'yang warnanya hitam' or 'yang berwarna hitam', never 'yang hitam warnanya' in the canonical line.

Address terms: at most one address term per turn, used only where a native would; omission is natural and allowed; Mas/Mbak for visibly young staff and friends-of-friends, Pak/Bu as default; never 'Anda' plus 'kamu' in one path.
Loanwords: diskon, garansi, konfirmasi, kursus, jadwal are Indonesian; antre (not antri) is the KBBI form; exemption per lesson id.
Derived trophies kehujanan and ketinggalan are new lexemes (caught in rain; left behind/missed), not evasions of the A1/A2 trophies hujan and tinggal; mesin, hasil and other roots stay bare.
Spoken numbers: rupiah amounts spoken in full (dua ratus ribu), times with jam only when needed and jam itself is a frozen A1 trophy, so never a B1 trophy.

Speech recognizer: id-ID B1 keeps the inherited 0.65 threshold and recording window until a measured pilot with the guidedSpeechCheck scorer; any longer window for 8-16 word lines is set from pilot data, not here.
mechanicalValidationRules: Exactly 10 paths × 10 lessons; lesson ids follow the frozen pattern indonesian-b1-<pathslug>-<n>-<nnn>-<trophy-slug> and never reuse an A1/A2 id.
Trophy set: 100 strings, NFC + casefold unique against each other and the full A1+A2 trophy list; regex ^[a-z]+$ (no hyphen, apostrophe, space, digit).

Trophy appears as a whitespace/punctuation-bounded token in corePhrase.targetText (first reply), in at least one pattern example targetText and in trophyWord.example; -nya/-lah/-kah suffixed occurrences do not count.
chunks.join(' ') === corePhrase.targetText; 4 ≤ chunks.length ≤ 7; no chunk is a lone function word unless it equals the staged connector of that lesson.
speakRequired: exactly 3 distinct lowercase tokens, each a whole-word match in the first reply, none in {pak,bu,mbak,mas,bapak,ibu,saya,anda,kamu,aku}.
First reply word count 8-16, second reply 6-12 (split on ASCII space after stripping punctuation).

Cloze: 2-3 blank parts on the second reply in the existing parts schema {kind: form|connector|choice, answer, cue?, choices[4]}; exactly one choice equals the removed surface token(s); blank ≤ 3 space-separated units; blank is never a lone token from {saya,anda,kamu,aku,dia,kita,kami,mereka,itu,ini,yang}; cue optional.
Recall: reconstructs first reply, 4 choices, blank is a content word or staged connector, never an address term or pronoun.

Base-tense licence: a line whose authored de/en tense tag is past/perfect/future must contain one of {sudah, tadi, kemarin, waktu itu, dulu, pernah, akan, mau, nanti, besok, tahun depan, minggu depan}; telah counts only in interlocutor or pattern lines; lalu/kemudian/setelah itu/akhirnya never satisfy this check.

Register lexicon: service-path learner lines must not contain kamu/aku; friend-path learner lines must not contain Anda; banned everywhere in learner lines: gue, lu, nggak, gak, banget, dong, sih, kok, awak, sila, tandas, macam, boleh tak, kalian as singular. No pronoun or address term is ever required to be present.

Staged-form gate: a grammatical form named in staging.productive (e.g. passive di- from P6 L1-4) may not appear in any learner line of an earlier path or earlier lesson; recognitionOnly forms may appear only in interlocutor or pattern lines. Ordinary vocabulary (nouns, plain verbs, adjectives) is not staged; only named forms are gated.
Co-occurrence ban (mechanical): 'walaupun|meskipun' with 'tetapi|tapi|namun' in one sentence. Irrealis consequence after seandainya and relativiser stacking are semantic review items, not regex.
Both de and en present on every base field; pedagogicalGoal is a German string; caption quotes the opening Indonesian line verbatim inside both locales.

Caption: both locales contain the opening Indonesian line verbatim and no verbatim quote of the follow-up line; absence of future leakage (facts known only after the follow-up) is a semantic review check, not a token diff.
Spoken numbers: digits forbidden in targetText, interlocutor lines, pattern examples; allowed in captions/situations.
semanticReviewRules: Follow-up turn adds a genuinely new fact, objection or constraint; a mere acknowledgement (Oh begitu) fails.

Shape C: learner's second reply accepts the staff proposal with one explicit modification; learner never states that a refund, room change or cancellation 'is done' (only staff decides); learner may request, propose, ask whether.
Shape A: complication is plausible and resolvable in one learner turn; resolution uses the path's family, not an unrelated form.
Shape B: learner's two replies form one connected narrative or argument (same topic, anaphoric link such as itu/tadi/setelah itu).
Concession lessons: the conceded point and the main point must genuinely conflict; reviewer rejects pseudo-concessions.

Hypothetical lessons: counterfactuals use seandainya only with irrealis consequence; soft requests use kalau boleh / kalau tidak keberatan / mohon + verb with a real request; sekiranya appears only in interlocutor or pattern lines.

Cloze choices: the three wrong choices are grammatical-looking builds (wrong negation, wrong aspect marker, wrong connector, wrong register) and none is a synonym that would also fit; reviewer checks every blank against a native reading.
Base parity: German and English carry the same aspect and politeness; German Konjunktiv II only where Indonesian has seandainya/sekiranya/kalau; otherwise indicative.

Pattern examples: 2-3 lines, highlight is one contiguous span of the target line containing the staged form; at least one example is the actual learner reply and contains the trophy; others recycle earlier-path vocabulary.
No Malay, no Jakarta slang, no calqued German word order (verb-final, 'doch', 'mal' equivalents).
Recycling honoured: each lesson's second reply reuses at least one form from the stated recycles field.

Trophy naturalness: trophy carries the communicative weight of the first reply; reviewer rejects incidental trophies. Derived trophies (ter-, ke-an, di-) pass when the reviewer confirms a distinct lexical meaning from the root and from every A1/A2 trophy.
requiredSchemaExtensions: Existing identities unchanged: dialogue tuple4, cloze parts string|{kind:form|connector|choice,answer,cue?,choices[4]}, pattern{label,rule,examples[{targetText,baseText,highlight}]}, recall{before,answer,after,fallbackChoices}, speakRequired[3], trophyWord{word,meaning,example,whyThisWord}. The existing B1 enum in exporters is reused.
Indonesian registration: id-ID B1 added wherever language/level codes are enumerated for lesson bodies and pickers; no new episode fields.

Native validator rules for id-ID: trophy regex ^[a-z]+$, banned-lexicon list, licensing-marker list, walaupun/tetapi co-occurrence, digits-in-speech check, address/pronoun exclusion from speakRequired and recall.
Optional reviewed accepted-variant metadata: acceptedVariants?: string[] per lesson, hand-reviewed, never rule-generated.
Staging metadata, loanword exemptions, derived-trophy root notes and per-line base tense tags live in this external spec and validator config, not in the app schema.

paths.title: Cerita Akhir Pekan
paths.anchor: Telling a friend what happened on a weekend trip to Yogyakarta and the coast

staging.productive: sequencing lalu / kemudian / setelah itu with an explicit time anchor in the same line (tadi, kemarin, waktu itu); background sedang; accidental ter- as lexical item (tersesat)
ketika / waktu + clause; sambil for simultaneous actions; mendadak / tiba-tiba as event markers
adversative ke-an (ketinggalan, kehujanan); akhirnya closing with its own past marker

paths.clozeSchema: Blanks on the sequencing connector, the time anchor and one aspect marker (sedang/sudah); distractors are other connectors or markers that break sequence.
paths.recycles: A2 P3 sudah/belum/tadi; A2 P4 mau/nanti; A1 place vocabulary (pasar, stasiun, pantai).

lessons.beat: Friend asks how Saturday started; you walked to the station, she asks where next.
You describe the morning market; friend asks what you bought there.
You admit getting lost in the old town; friend asks who helped you.
You recall crossing the bridge while it drizzled; friend asks about photos.
You reached the beach at sunset while eating; friend asks about the water.
Suddenly the bus did not come; friend asks how you got back.
You dropped by a warung on the way; friend asks what was tasty.
You missed the last train; friend asks where you slept.
You got soaked walking to the hostel; friend asks if you fell ill.
Finally home Sunday night; friend asks whether you would go again.

paths.title: Menurut Saya
paths.anchor: Discussing films, food and city life with a friend who often disagrees

staging.productive: menurut saya / pendapat saya; setuju / tidak setuju; sebenarnya
walaupun / meskipun + clause; tetapi contrast in separate sentence; terlalu + adjective
memang ... tetapi / tapi ya; namun as sentence opener; comparative lebih recycled with concession

paths.clozeSchema: Blanks on the concession connector, the stance word (setuju/memang/sebenarnya) and degree word (terlalu/lebih); distractors are connectors producing the wrong logic.
paths.recycles: A2 P2 lebih + adjective, karena; A1 enak, bagus, menarik contexts; P1 sequencing in anecdotes.

lessons.beat: Friend asks about last night's film; you give your view, she asks why.
Friend asks your opinion on the new café; she probes the prices.
Friend says city traffic is hopeless; you partly agree, she asks solutions.
You liked the beach although crowded; friend asks about a quieter spot.
Friend assumes you love spicy food; you correct her, she asks favourites.
You found the museum interesting despite the heat; friend asks what stood out.
You call the series boring though well acted; friend defends the plot.
Friend suggests the mall; you find it too expensive, she proposes a market.
Friend says rent downtown is reasonable; you argue it's expensive, she compares areas.
Friend criticises your neighbourhood; you concede the noise yet praise neighbours, she asks more.

paths.title: Kalau Boleh
paths.anchor: Soft requests and hypotheticals at a guesthouse front desk and a travel agency

staging.productive: kalau boleh / boleh saya + verb; maaf mengganggu opener; tolong + verb; menukar and pilihan lain as request vocabulary
mohon + verb polite request; kalau tidak keberatan; kalau bisa; menunda as request verb
seandainya + irrealis consequence (saya akan / mungkin); membatalkan as request verb; ada tambahan / diskon questions

paths.clozeSchema: Blanks on the request softener, the request verb and the hypothetical connector; distractors include realis kalau vs irrealis seandainya mismatches.
paths.recycles: A2 P1 service formulas; A1 reservasi, kamar, sewa; P2 tetapi for polite objection.

lessons.beat: Receptionist greets you; you apologise for disturbing and ask about late checkout, she offers noon.
Clerk asks how to help; you ask to swap rooms, he offers a different floor.
Agent lists one tour; you ask for other options, she suggests a morning one.
You politely request (mohon disiapkan) an early breakfast; staff offers a packed box.
You ask whether they'd mind storing bags; clerk sets a time limit.
You ask to postpone the tour a day; agent mentions a small fee.
You ask what would happen if you cancelled; agent explains partial refund.
You consider cancelling the second night; receptionist proposes keeping it cheaper.
You ask about an extra bed; staff offers one with surcharge.
You ask whether a discount exists for three nights; agent counters with breakfast included.

paths.title: Yang Warnanya Hitam
paths.anchor: Describing lost items, people and places at a lost-and-found desk and a mall information point

staging.productive: yang + adjective; yang warnanya + colour; berwarna + colour
yang + verb clause (yang saya bawa, yang tertinggal di meja); ber- descriptive (bergaris, berkantong); bentuk / ukuran descriptions
terbuat dari + material; result ter- (tertulis, tertempel); pemilik / milik ownership phrasing

paths.clozeSchema: Blanks on yang vs. bare adjective choice, the ber-/ter- descriptive and the material/possessive phrase; distractors are wrong relativiser placements or wrong prefix.
paths.recycles: A1 colours and sizes; A2 P2 yang ini / yang itu; P1 tadi / kemarin for when the item was lost.

lessons.beat: Staff asks what you lost; you describe a black bag, she finds two black bags.
Staff asks the colour of the umbrella; yours is green, hers is blue.
You describe a brown wallet; staff asks about contents to verify.
You report a jacket left at the café; staff found one without hood.
You describe glasses in a red case; staff shows a similar black case.
Staff asks about a striped shirt; yours is striped blue, theirs is plain.
Staff asks the shape of the box; you say round, she shows square.
You say the bracelet is made of silver; staff asks for identifying marks.
You describe a wide wooden tray; staff asks whether it had a sticker.
You ask about the owner of a found phone; staff asks you to describe where.

paths.title: Saya Ingin Tahu
paths.anchor: Indirect enquiries at a clinic registration, a bank counter and a city office

staging.productive: boleh saya tanya + question word; saya ingin tahu + kapan / di mana; embedded question word order
saya ingin tahu apakah ...; Anda tahu apakah ...; jadwal / biaya / syarat as enquiry nouns
apakah ... masih berlaku; harus mendaftar + where/when; antre procedures with sebelum/setelah

paths.clozeSchema: Blanks on the embedding verb (tahu/tanya), the embedded question word or apakah, and the enquiry noun; distractors swap direct for indirect order.
paths.recycles: A1 jam/menit for schedules; A2 P1 kartu / tagihan; P3 kalau boleh softener before enquiry.

lessons.beat: Clinic clerk asks your business; you ask when the doctor arrives, she says delayed.
You want to know where to register; clerk sends you upstairs, system down.
You ask when results are ready; nurse says tomorrow, you need them today.
You ask whether the bank opens Saturday; teller says only mornings.
You ask about the counselling schedule; officer says it changed this week.
You ask the cost of a new card; teller adds an unexpected stamp fee.
You ask the requirements for a permit; clerk needs a document you lack.
You ask whether your visa is still valid; officer spots an expiring date.
You ask where to register online; clerk says the site is down, offers paper.
You ask whether you must queue again; officer explains a priority window.

paths.title: Sudah Diproses
paths.anchor: Following up on processes and results at a repair shop, a courier office and a bank

staging.productive: agentless di- passive with sudah/belum (sudah diperiksa, belum dikirim); selesai as result
di- passive with oleh agent; ternyata result reveal; hasil + possessive
gagal / berhasil + verb; mesin and system subjects with di- passive; konfirmasi request (minta konfirmasi)

paths.recycles: A2 P3 sudah/belum bayar; A2 P9 rusak / perbaiki contexts; P5 apakah embedded for status questions.

lessons.beat: Technician asks your ticket number; you ask if the laptop was checked, part missing.
You ask whether the parcel was sent; clerk says address incomplete.
You ask if the repair is finished; technician needs one more day.
You ask whether your transfer is processed; teller says pending verification.
You report the phone still fails; technician says battery turned out faulty.

You request written confirmation of the repair; staff can only send tomorrow.

paths.title: Supaya Lancar
paths.anchor: Planning a hiking weekend and a budget with a friend, with purposes and conditions

staging.productive: untuk + verb purpose; supaya + clause; kalau + condition with akan/mau consequence; libur / cuaca planning nouns
agar as formal purpose; jika + condition; asalkan condition-with-concession
membawa / menghemat in plan statements; combined purpose + condition in one turn (kalau ..., supaya ...); mendaki itinerary

paths.clozeSchema: Blanks on the purpose connector, the condition connector and the future licence (akan/mau); distractors swap purpose for cause (karena) or realis for irrealis.
paths.recycles: A2 P4 mau / bagaimana kalau; P3 seandainya recognition; P1 sequencing for itinerary.

Friend asks when you are off; you name the long weekend, she suggests Friday.

Friend wants the higher mountain; you prefer the lower one, she proposes both.
You plan to hike at dawn; friend suggests a guide for safety.
You list what to bring to save money; friend asks who carries water.
You propose sharing a car to save; friend agrees if you drive back.

paths.title: Dulu dan Kini
paths.anchor: Comparing childhood habits and current routines with a friend over tea

staging.productive: dulu ... sekarang contrast; pernah for experience; masih for continuing
tidak ... lagi; jarang / setiap frequency; sejak + time or clause; olahraga as activity noun
kebiasaan + possessive; berubah with sejak; sudah tidak + verb lagi; berenang as hobby verb

paths.title: Setahun Ini

staging.productive: selama + duration; past narration with sudah/pernah recycled; pengalaman + yang clause; kursus as milestone noun
future plans with tahun depan / akan / berencana-free framing (saya mau); menabung untuk; lulus milestone; terus + verb continuation
semoga + hope clause; harapan saya + clause; bersyukur karena closing

unresolvedDecisions: Resolved: friend-path canonical lines may use saya, aku or pronoun omission as natural; the other pronoun is a reviewed accepted variant where the line stays identical in meaning.
Resolved: derived-form trophies (tersesat, kehujanan, ketinggalan, terbuat, diperiksa, dikirim, diproses, diantar) are legal distinct lexemes under the non-evasion rule; roots stay bare elsewhere.
Resolved: sekiranya is recognition-only at B1; P3 L4 trophy is mohon.
